response:
It sounds like you're carrying a lot of hurt, and it's completely understandable. When someone close to us repeatedly criticizes our character, it can be deeply painful and confusing, even when we know they care about us.

It's worth trusting your own instincts here. If you haven't received this feedback from others in your life, it may say more about your cousin's communication style and emotional regulation than about who you are. Her temper and frustration don't give her the right to belittle you, regardless of her intentions.

Since direct conversation hasn't worked and tends to circle back to attacks, you might consider setting clearer boundaries around what you will and won't accept. It's okay to say something like, "I want to spend time together, but I need you to speak to me respectfully." You can also limit how much emotional energy you give to her criticisms, recognizing that her comments reflect her perspective, not your worth.

Your feelings are valid, and prioritizing your emotional well-being is not inconsiderate—it's healthy.
